title: Next Permutation
description:
A permutation of an array of integers is an arrangement of its elements into a sequence. The next permutation of an array is the lexicographically next greater permutation of its elements.

If no greater permutation exists (meaning the array is sorted in non-increasing order), rearrange `nums` into the lowest possible order (sorted in non-decreasing order).

The replacement must be done in-place and use only `O(1)` extra memory.
hints: Scan from right to left to find the first index i (the pivot) where nums[i] < nums[i + 1]. Everything to the right of i is already non-increasing.
If such an index i exists, scan from the right end to find the rightmost index j > i with nums[j] > nums[i], and swap nums[i] with nums[j].
Finally, reverse the suffix starting at i + 1 (or the entire array if no pivot existed) to make that suffix as small as possible.

examples.explanation: The lexicographically next permutation after [1, 2, 3] is [1, 3, 2].
[3, 2, 1] is the largest permutation, so it wraps around to [1, 2, 3].
Swapping the pivot 1 at index 1 with 5 gives [1, 5, 1].
